rv.q: County Hall's high-domed Council Chamber...has been turned into the courthouse for an enthralling Lucy Bailey revival of this 1953 play.
Convention says that TV has now appropriated this kind of Christie mystery but, when staged as cleverly as this, her plays can still work with a live audience.
Combined with Bailey’s inspired use of an historic location, it’s criminally entertaining.
The debating chamber of the old Greater London Council lends a genuine touch of majesty to proceedings.
This interpretation is a bit slow-footed by comparison and lacks a nagging element of mystery.
This juicy Witness looks set to be giving evidence for a long time.
The production struggles more in the intimate scenes in legal chambers and falls awkwardly flat in the one episode outside the court.
But ultimately the production resembles something you might catch on ITV3 in the early afternoon.
It’s difficult to imagine how anybody could not enjoy this play.
A fantastic cast and creative team combine to make a truly thrilling piece of theatre that's an experience as much as a show - a theatrical jury service you'll never forget.
Witness for the Prosecution is a really entertaining play.
Guilty of being a good night out.
All in all, it’s a quintessentially British affair that will appeal to fans of period drama and murder mysteries.
Go for the playhouse if not wholly for the play.
It’s a story that does manage to engage for the most part, but needs a few more gear changes.
But the on-stage efforts struggle to match the authenticity and genuine drama of the extraordinary environment.
All in all, Witness for the Prosecution is a spine-tingling and mesmerising watch which messes with your mind perfectly.
This production is enormously impressive, offering a classic thriller in an extraordinary setting that elevates the play beyond its already superb script.
The queen of cunning has been brilliantly served.
This production and setting find the perfect expression of a strong storyline
This is one of the most unique theatrical experiences available right now, and you will not be disappointed.

cn.t: Christie's courtroom thriller gets compelling new life in Lucy Bailey's site-specific staging at County Hall's grand chamber, which critics agree is the production's star attraction, though some find the vast space works against the drama's intimacy.

lo.inst: Enter via InYouGo/show website. Draws Wednesdays.

dr.inst: Released @ 10 AM via TodayTix app only.

vr.q: It turns out to be a very satisfactory evening, well put together, well acted and well produced in a striking venue.
